cleanIntro:
The Timberwolf is Lone Wolf's striker-fired pistol. It has no manual safety: a trigger safety lever, a firing pin safety and a drop safety are built in, and it fires whenever the trigger is pulled with a round in the chamber.

Lone Wolf's field strip takes it to five pieces: magazine, frame, barrel, guide rod assembly and slide. The slide comes off forward with the slide lock lever held down, after the trigger has been pressed on an empty chamber. The book stops there for cleaning.

This guide follows Lone Wolf's own TIMBERWOLF Owners Manual. Wear safety glasses for the strip and the clean.

steps.title: Ammunition away, magazine out
steps.action: Move all ammunition away from where you are working. Point the pistol in a safe direction, press the magazine catch and pull the magazine out. If it is loaded, unload it and put those rounds out of the area too. Taking the magazine out does not make the pistol safe: a round can still be in the chamber.
steps.quote: While pointing the pistol in a safe direction, depress the magazine catch and remove the magazine.
steps.cite: Lone Wolf TIMBERWOLF Owners Manual — UNKNOWN — no revision or document number is printed; the last page carries only "7.31.24", unlabelled — FIELD STRIPPING, Magazine Removal, p.17
steps.warn: WARNING: PISTOL IS CAPABLE OF FIRING WITHOUT A MAGAZINE.

steps.title: Rack it three times, lock it open
steps.action: Pull the slide back and let it go three times to throw out anything in the chamber. On the last pull, lock the slide open. The slide must stay locked back for the check that follows.
steps.quote: Pull back the slide to rack it three times and then lock the slide in the open position.
steps.cite: Lone Wolf TIMBERWOLF Owners Manual — UNKNOWN — no revision or document number is printed; the last page carries only "7.31.24", unlabelled — VERIFICATION OF EMPTY PISTOL, p.18

steps.title: Look, then feel the chamber with your little finger
steps.action: Look into the chamber and the magazine well. Then put your little finger into the chamber and feel that it is empty. Lone Wolf asks for both: the eye can miss a case that the finger cannot. Do not knock the slide stop lever while your finger is in there.
steps.quote: Using your little finger, physically verify that the chamber is clear.
steps.cite: Lone Wolf TIMBERWOLF Owners Manual — UNKNOWN — no revision or document number is printed; the last page carries only "7.31.24", unlabelled — VERIFICATION OF EMPTY PISTOL, p.18
steps.warn: WHEN USING YOUR LITTLE FINGER TO CHECK THE CHAMBER, BE CERTAIN THAT THE SLIDE IS LOCKED IN THE OPEN POSITION.

steps.title: Slide forward on an empty chamber
steps.action: Keep the muzzle in a safe direction and let the slide go forward on the empty chamber. Look at the extractor on the slide: on this pistol it is the loaded chamber indicator. Flush with the slide means the chamber is empty; if it sticks out, a round is chambered, so stop and clear the pistol again.
steps.aside: The extractor will be flush with the slide when the chamber is empty and will stick out when a round is in the chamber.
steps.quote: While ensuring the chamber remains empty and the firearm is pointed in a safe direction, release the slide.
steps.cite: Lone Wolf TIMBERWOLF Owners Manual — UNKNOWN — no revision or document number is printed; the last page carries only "7.31.24", unlabelled — RELEASE THE SLIDE, p.19

steps.title: Press the trigger, muzzle in a safe direction
steps.action: With the slide closed on the empty chamber, point the pistol in a safe direction and press the trigger. You will hear the firing pin go forward. The slide cannot come off until this is done, and it is why the chamber had to be checked twice first.
steps.aside: You will hear the firing pin move forward.
steps.quote: Now that the slide is closed, point the pistol in a safe direction and depress the trigger.
steps.cite: Lone Wolf TIMBERWOLF Owners Manual — UNKNOWN — no revision or document number is printed; the last page carries only "7.31.24", unlabelled — REMOVE THE SLIDE, p.20

steps.title: Muzzle down, slide back 1/8 to 1/4 inch
steps.action: Hold the muzzle with your left hand (right-handed) and turn the pistol so the barrel points at the floor. Wrap your right palm and fingers over the slide with your right thumb on the backstrap of the grip. Press down with the thumb so the slide moves back only about 1/8 to 1/4 inch. Go further and the trigger resets, and you start again from the trigger press.
steps.quote: Apply downward pressure with right thumb, moving the slide approximately 1/8” to 1/4”.
steps.cite: Lone Wolf TIMBERWOLF Owners Manual — UNKNOWN — no revision or document number is printed; the last page carries only "7.31.24", unlabelled — REMOVE THE SLIDE, p.20
steps.warn: IF THE SLIDE IS MOVED REARWARD MORE THAN ¼” YOU WILL HEAR THE TRIGGER RESET AND YOU MUST START THE SLIDE REMOVAL PROCESS AGAIN.

steps.title: Slide lock lever down, slide off the front
steps.action: Hold the slide back that short distance. With your left hand around the trigger guard, pull both sides of the slide lock lever down at the same time, thumb on one side and middle finger on the other. Keep the lever down and push the slide forward until it comes clear of the frame. Both sides of the lever stay down until the slide is off.
steps.aside: simultaneously pull down both sides of the slide lock lever with your left thumb and middle finger.
steps.quote: Maintain downward pressure of the slide lock lever and push the slide forward until it is fully separated from the receiver.
steps.cite: Lone Wolf TIMBERWOLF Owners Manual — UNKNOWN — no revision or document number is printed; the last page carries only "7.31.24", unlabelled — REMOVE THE SLIDE, p.20

steps.title: Guide rod assembly out of the slide
steps.action: Turn the slide over and rest the muzzle in the palm of your hand. With your index finger or thumb, push the guide rod assembly forward and to the side to lift it out. Lone Wolf asks for caution here: keep hold of the assembly as it comes free.
steps.quote: Place muzzle in palm of your hand - while exercising caution - and using your index finger or thumb, push the guide rod assembly forward and to the side, removing it from the assembly.
steps.cite: Lone Wolf TIMBERWOLF Owners Manual — UNKNOWN — no revision or document number is printed; the last page carries only "7.31.24", unlabelled — BARREL REMOVAL, p.21

steps.title: Barrel out by the lug
steps.action: Take hold of the barrel by its lug, the block under the chamber end. Lift it up and forward, then out of the slide. The guide rod assembly comes out first; the barrel follows it.
steps.quote: Grasp the barrel by the lug, lift it up and forward then out from the slide.
steps.cite: Lone Wolf TIMBERWOLF Owners Manual — UNKNOWN — no revision or document number is printed; the last page carries only "7.31.24", unlabelled — BARREL REMOVAL, p.21

steps.title: Field strip complete: five pieces
steps.action: You now have five pieces: the empty magazine, the frame, the barrel, the guide rod assembly and the slide. That is as far as Lone Wolf takes the pistol apart for cleaning. Its other pages (magwell, backstrap, ejector, adapter, magazine catch) are for customizing the pistol, not cleaning it, and this guide does not follow them.
steps.prose: Lone Wolf asks for lubrication about every 2,000 rounds, on the slide where it rubs against other metal parts.
steps.quote: NO FURTHER DISASSEMBLY IS REQUIRED FOR BASIC CLEANING AND MAINTENANCE
steps.cite: Lone Wolf TIMBERWOLF Owners Manual — UNKNOWN — no revision or document number is printed; the last page carries only "7.31.24", unlabelled — BARREL REMOVAL, NOTE, p.21

deepAbsentReason: There is no deep clean for the Timberwolf. Lone Wolf's TIMBERWOLF Owners Manual ends its cleaning disassembly at the field strip and says so ("NO FURTHER DISASSEMBLY IS REQUIRED FOR BASIC CLEANING AND MAINTENANCE", p.21). Its later pages, pp.23-27, cover customization only, and the ejector page starts from a trigger housing already out of the frame, a removal the book never describes. If any of the pistol's safeties seem not to work, Lone Wolf says to unload it and not use it until a Lone Wolf Certified Armorer has examined it (p.16).

cleaning.name: SLIDE
tasks: Extractor cleaned, paying attention to the extraction claw; replaced if needed
Firing pin cleaned; replaced if needed
Lubricated where the slide meets other metal parts, about every 2,000 rounds

cleaning.name: BARREL AND CHAMBER
tasks: Barrel looked over before it goes back in

cleaning.name: GUIDE ROD ASSEMBLY
tasks: Guide rod assembly inspected; replaced if needed

cleaning.name: FRAME
tasks: Trigger mechanism housing and ejector inspected; replaced if needed
Do not alter or modify the pistol's safeties

cleaning.name: MAGAZINE
tasks: Magazine inspected and cleaned; replaced if needed
Magazine spring replaced if the pistol fails to feed

cleaning.name: ⚠ BEFORE AND DURING
tasks: ⚠ Safety glasses on for the field strip and the cleaning
⚠ All ammunition out of the work area

reassembly: The book prints no reassembly sequence; put the pistol back together in the reverse order of the strip.
fncheck: Lone Wolf prints no function check. Before loading, look at the extractor with the slide closed on the empty chamber: Lone Wolf uses it as the loaded chamber indicator, flush with the slide when the chamber is empty (p.19). If any of the pistol's safeties seem not to work, the book says to unload it and not use it again until a Lone Wolf Certified Armorer has examined it (p.16). Use only factory-made ammunition in the pistol's own caliber; Lone Wolf says reloads void the warranty.
